newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU presidency says rights key to Turkish EU goal.
newsitem.headline: EU presidency says rights key to Turkish EU goal.

text.p: Turkey must improve its human rights and solve its conflict with the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) peacefully if it wants to join the European Union, the EU presidency said on Wednesday.

"Turkey must be judged by the same benchmarks and objective criteria as the other candidates for (EU) accession," said Luxembourg Secretary of State Georges Wohlfart, whose country took over the rotating six-month EU presidency on July 1.

He was speaking at the European Parliament on the day the European Commission, the bloc's Brussels-based executive, recommended the EU open negotiations in early 1998 with six out of 10 European countries seeking Union membership.
Turkey was not among the six, whose eligibility to join the EU early next century hinges on their commitment to democracy, respect of human rights and a market economy.
"Respect of human rights and democracy in Turkey will continue to be the centre of the (EU's) concerns," Wohlfart told the EU assembly.
The European Parliament is expected on Thursday to pass a resolution condemning Turkey's incursions into northern Iraq against the PKK and calling for an immediate withdrawl of Ankara's troops.
"The Kurdish issue can only be resolved by political not military means," Wohlfart said.
On May 17, EU governments called on Turkey to pull its military forces out of northern Iraq as soon as possible and warned against any loss of civilian life.
Turkish troops, tanks and air power have pounded rebel Kurdish positions inside northern Iraq in an assault by at least 10,000 troops in a remote mountainous region against camps of the PKK in Iraq.
Cyprus, divided between its Turkish and Greek communities for the last two decades, was among the six countries the Commission said was ready to start negotiating EU membership next year.
